artwork_title: A Small Chinese Sancai Glazed 'Double Fish' Vase, Tang Dynasty
provenance: Formerly collection of Jürgen L. Fischer. The extensive size of the collection is largely owed to the family’s fortune, secured by pharmacist August Fischer and his revolutionary invention – the world’s first adhesive made from synthetic resin, the famous “Uhu Alleskleber”, developed in 1932. Jürgen L. Fischer lived until 2013 and was an avid collector of Chinese porcelain whose astonishing taste encompassed a broad spectrum of types, of all sizes and with origins spanning across millennia. Jürgen Fischer passed on his comprehensive knowledge in numerous text books – among others, his large and very instructive book about the art of Chinese snuffbottles and also an antiquarian’s guide to Chinese art. Acquired from Galerie Zacke, Vienna, Austria, June 4, 2016, Fine Asian Art, Lot 41.

Property from the estate of Rafeeuddin Ahmed, New York, New York.Mr. Rafeeuddin Ahmed had a long and distinguished diplomatic career, serving with the Pakistan Foreign Service from 1955-1969, and in 1970 embarked on the first of several distinguished roles within the United Nations Secretariat, spanning over 30 years. Between 1955 and 1968, he served at the Embassies of Cairo, Ottawa, and Beijing. Mr. Ahmed was highly respected by colleagues and those who came to know him. He was a valued mentor and a great believer in the power of multilateralism and international cooperation, and, as a tribute from the World Tourism Organization (UN Tourism) notes, “…leaving behind a legacy defined not only by institutional achievement, but by humanity, wisdom and grace.”来源：纽约市外交家拉菲乌丁·艾哈迈德（Rafeeuddin Ahmed，1932—2026）遗产。巴基斯坦资深外交家艾哈迈德供职于联合国体系逾三十年，以副秘书长级别工作二十一年，是国际多边外交领域的重要人物之一。艾氏毕业于巴基斯坦旁遮普大学，后赴美国塔夫茨大学深造，专攻国际经济与国际法。1954年他以政治学讲师身份开启职业生涯，次年加入巴基斯坦外交部，1955至1969年间先后派驻开罗、渥太华及北京等地。1970年进入联合国秘书处，历任开发计划署高级顾问、经济及社会理事会秘书、秘书长办公厅主任、亚太经济社会委员会执行秘书等职。艾氏多次受命处理复杂国际事务，参与过东帝汶、柬埔寨、老挝—泰国冲突及缅甸等地区的调停。在1982年福克兰群岛危机和伊朗人质事件中发挥了重要作用。2003年又被任命为伊拉克问题特别顾问。他在2026年逝世，一生成就卓著，评价极高。本场委托的中国艺术品购自1960年代派驻北京巴基斯坦使馆任内。

Property from the Collection of George C.T. Wan, New York, thence by descent.George Chien-Tze ("C.T.") Wan was born in Jiangxi province, of China. He became interested in Chinese porcelains when, in Shanghai, Mr. Wan worked as a representative for importers of Chinese porcelains to the United States. Through this work, he obtained sponsorship to immigrate to the United States in 1949. Within a year, C.T. Wan & Co., dealer in Chinese art and antiques, was inaugurated in New York City at 116 East 28th St. Thus began a dedication and passion for Asian art and collecting that was to fulfill Mr. Wan's excellent life until his passing in 2019. The store moved twice, first a few blocks away to 235 Fifth Avenue in the 1960's and then across the avenue in the 1980's to 242 Fifth Avenue. In the 2000’s, surrounded by his collection, Mr. Wan would smile and reflect on what great satisfaction and pride his life's work had brought to him.來源：萬寶古董行庫藏。該行由江西籍古董商萬氏創立，萬氏上世紀中葉在滬從事瓷器出口貿易，1949年移民紐約，于28街東116號經營瓷器，店名C.T. Wan & Co，后遷五大道235號，再遷242號。店址雖多次變動，都位於五大道與28街交匯處，這是當年紐約亞洲藝術交易的中心，如山中商會就在254號，與萬寶古董行一街之隔。千禧年后，萬氏年高，淡出經營，2019年下世，本次上拍子女繼承的部分庫存。

Property from the Collection of George C.T. Wan, New York, thence by descent.George Chien-Tze ("C.T.") Wan was born in Jiangxi province, of China. He became interested in Chinese porcelains when, in Shanghai, Mr. Wan worked as a representative for importers of Chinese porcelains to the United States. Through this work, he obtained sponsorship to immigrate to the United States in 1949. Within a year, C.T. Wan & Co., dealer in Chinese art and antiques, was inaugurated in New York City at 116 East 28th St. Thus began a dedication and passion for Asian art and collecting that was to fulfill Mr. Wan's excellent life until his passing in 2019. The store moved twice, first a few blocks away to 235 Fifth Avenue in the 1960's and then across the avenue in the 1980's to 242 Fifth Avenue. In the 2000’s, surrounded by his collection, Mr. Wan would smile and reflect on what great satisfaction and pride his life's work had brought to him.來源：萬寶古董行庫藏。該行由江西籍古董商萬氏創立，萬氏上世紀中葉在滬從事瓷器出口貿易，1949年移民紐約，于28街東116號經營瓷器，店名C.T. Wan & Co，后遷五大道235號，再遷242號。店址雖多次變動，都位於五大道與28街交匯處，這是當年紐約亞洲藝術交易的中心，如山中商會就在254號，與萬寶古董行一街之隔。千禧年后，萬氏年高，淡出經營，2019年下世，本次上拍子女繼承的部分庫存。

Property from the Collection of George C.T. Wan, New York, thence by descent.George Chien-Tze ("C.T.") Wan was born in Jiangxi province, of China. He became interested in Chinese porcelains when, in Shanghai, Mr. Wan worked as a representative for importers of Chinese porcelains to the United States. Through this work, he obtained sponsorship to immigrate to the United States in 1949. Within a year, C.T. Wan & Co., dealer in Chinese art and antiques, was inaugurated in New York City at 116 East 28th St. Thus began a dedication and passion for Asian art and collecting that was to fulfill Mr. Wan's excellent life until his passing in 2019. The store moved twice, first a few blocks away to 235 Fifth Avenue in the 1960's and then across the avenue in the 1980's to 242 Fifth Avenue. In the 2000’s, surrounded by his collection, Mr. Wan would smile and reflect on what great satisfaction and pride his life's work had brought to him.來源：萬寶古董行庫藏。該行由江西籍古董商萬氏創立，萬氏上世紀中葉在滬從事瓷器出口貿易，1949年移民紐約，于28街東116號經營瓷器，店名C.T. Wan & Co，后遷五大道235號，再遷242號。店址雖多次變動，都位於五大道與28街交匯處，這是當年紐約亞洲藝術交易的中心，如山中商會就在254號，與萬寶古董行一街之隔。千禧年后，萬氏年高，淡出經營，2019年下世，本次上拍子女繼承的部分庫存。

Property from the Collection of George C.T. Wan, New York, thence by descent.George Chien-Tze ("C.T.") Wan was born in Jiangxi province, of China. He became interested in Chinese porcelains when, in Shanghai, Mr. Wan worked as a representative for importers of Chinese porcelains to the United States. Through this work, he obtained sponsorship to immigrate to the United States in 1949. Within a year, C.T. Wan & Co., dealer in Chinese art and antiques, was inaugurated in New York City at 116 East 28th St. Thus began a dedication and passion for Asian art and collecting that was to fulfill Mr. Wan's excellent life until his passing in 2019. The store moved twice, first a few blocks away to 235 Fifth Avenue in the 1960's and then across the avenue in the 1980's to 242 Fifth Avenue. In the 2000’s, surrounded by his collection, Mr. Wan would smile and reflect on what great satisfaction and pride his life's work had brought to him.來源：萬寶古董行庫藏。該行由江西籍古董商萬氏創立，萬氏上世紀中葉在滬從事瓷器出口貿易，1949年移民紐約，于28街東116號經營瓷器，店名C.T. Wan & Co，后遷五大道235號，再遷242號。店址雖多次變動，都位於五大道與28街交匯處，這是當年紐約亞洲藝術交易的中心，如山中商會就在254號，與萬寶古董行一街之隔。千禧年后，萬氏年高，淡出經營，2019年下世，本次上拍子女繼承的部分庫存。

provenance: Property from the Estate of Dr. Thomas A. Klein, MD. Sold to benefit the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at Thomas Jefferson University Hospital.
description_block:
Two Chinese Porcelain Figural Snuff Bottles
粉彩瓷雕人物鼻烟壺兩支

-The first second half of the 19th century. Molded in the form of Li Tieguai wearing a robe and holding a staff, a double gourd on his back hollowed as a snuff bottle, enameled in black and white with iron-red accents, the base flat.
-The second 19th/20th century, molded as a smiling “reclining lady,” finely painted in famille-rose colors, one foot containing the stopper

Tallest height with stopper 3 9/16 in., 9.0 cm.

Property from the Estate of Dr. Thomas Klein, sold to benefit Jefferson Hospital

This lot is located in Philadelphia.
-Male: Galerie Zacke, Vienna, March 9, 2023, lot 602 -Female: Asiantiques, New Orleans, 2006 Property from the Estate of Dr. Thomas A. Klein, MD. Sold to benefit the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at Thomas Jefferson University Hospital. Thomas Klein醫生遺產，拍賣所得歸Jefferson醫院。湯姆·克萊因醫生收藏鼻烟壺逾四十年。他畢業於哈佛大學與羅徹斯特大學，曾於美國陸軍擔任婦產科醫師並出任高階領導職務。其後於傑佛遜醫院服務三十年，2023年以婦產科副主任身分榮退，期間培養了五百餘名住院醫師與無數醫學生。他的學術與臨床精神延續於以其名設立的「Thomas A. Klein 講席教授」，本場拍賣所得亦歸於傑佛遜醫院。Tom Klein’s life was shaped by two enduring passions: medicine and the collecting of snuff bottles. While these worlds rarely intersected, both were marked by the same qualities—quiet dedication, discernment, and grace. Tom was unfailingly modest–when the I.C.S.B.S. held its convention in Philadelphia, he entrusted me to select bottles from his collection for the exhibition “Embers of the East,” a task made challenging by the number of exceptional bottles. His passion for collecting was thoughtful rather than acquisitive, grounded in appreciation rather than display. These were his companions—objects he handled, studied, and loved for over 40 years.Professionally, Tom enjoyed an equally distinguished career. A graduate of Harvard University and the University of Rochester, he served as an obstetrician-gynecologist in the U.S. Army in senior leadership roles. He spent thirty years at Jefferson Hospital, retiring in 2023 as Vice Chair of Obstetrics and Gynecology, having trained more than five hundred residents and countless medical students. His legacy continues through the Thomas A. Klein, MD Professorship in Quality and Safety in Women’s Health. To those who knew him as a collector, these accomplishments mirrored the man I admired: principled, generous, and exacting without pretension. Over the 35 years I had the privilege to know him, he was a gentleman in the most absolute sense of the word. Though he is deeply missed, his presence endures in the objects he cherished and in our shared love of snuff bottles.Clare Chu

artwork_title: Five Chinese Porcelain and Stoneware Snuff Bottles 瓷鼻烟壺五支
provenance: Property from the Estate of Dr. Thomas A. Klein, sold to benefit Jefferson Hospital
description_block:
Five Chinese Porcelain and Stoneware Snuff Bottles
瓷鼻烟壺五支

-The first, 20th century, porcelain of cylindrical form with a waisted neck, gilt flat lip and flat base surrounded by a protruding circular footrim, the milk-white body well-painted in famille-rose colors to depict a continuous scene of boys in an outdoor setting, the base with an apocryphal four-character Qianlong nian zhi inscription in iron-red seal script.
-The second modern, of ovoid form, decorated with Zhongkui and bats, an inscription and two seals verso, underside with apocryphal Qianlong mark
-The third, circa 1820-1850. Enamelled Yixing stoneware of tapering ovoid form, with a cylindrical neck and flat lip, one side with a panel depicting a pavilion beneath a tree-covered peak, the reverse depicting a sage contemplating a landscape, all reserved on a ground imitating turquoise matrix or shagreen.
-The fourth, 19th/20th century. Porcelain of bulging meiping form, with an everted lipped neck, wide mouth and flat recessed base, the milk-white body painted in underglaze cobalt blue to depict a continuous scene of stylized lotus scrolls, the neck encircled with lingzhi motifs above a double ring, the base with a four-character Yongzheng nian zhi mark in regular script.
-The fifth, Mid-19th to 20th century. Porcelain small “pot” of squat form, with an everted lipped neck, very wide mouth and flat foot surrounded by a protruding circular footrim, the milk-white body painted in underglaze cobalt blue to depict the animals of the zodiac, the shoulders with bats, a blue ring beneath the lip and above the base, the base with a four-character Daoguang nian zhi mark in seal script, the interior also glazed. 

Tallest height with stopper 3 in., 7.6 cm.

Property from the Estate of Dr. Thomas Klein, sold to benefit Jefferson Hospital

玻璃内畫鼻烟壺四支

-The first, 20th/21st century, Glass of rounded-rectangular form, with a cylindrical neck, flat lip and protruding oval footrim, inside-painted to depict, on one main side, a very well-painted blue and white porcelain teapot, the reverse with a bronze censer, all against an even monochromatic buff background.
-The second, Late 19th/20th century, attributed to Ye Zhongsan. Glass of slightly bulbous rounded-rectangular form, with a cylindrical neck, flat lip and protruding oval footrim, inside-painted in shades of black, gray, white and russet to depict a continuous scene of the eight horses of Mu Wang in a pastoral landscape, with an inscription and seal of Ye Zhongsan.

A drizzling rain falls like tears on Mourning Day;
The mourner’s heart will break on his way.
Where can a wine shop be found to drown his sad hours?
A cowherd points to a cot amid apricot flowers

-The second, dated to a dingmao year (1963). Glass of tapering rounded-rectangular form, with a slightly waisted neck, flat lip and shallow protruding oval footrim, the body finely painted in black ink to depict, on one main side, a portrait of Ren Bonian (Ren Yi), the reverse with a lengthy biographical inscription.

provenance: Property from the Estate of Dr. Thomas A. Klein, MD. Sold to benefit the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at Thomas Jefferson University Hospital.
description_block:
Six Chinese Glass Overlay Snuff Bottles
套料鼻烟壺六支

-The first 19th/20th century, of bulging ovoid form, the shoulders sloping to a waisted neck, with a flat lip and base surrounded by a protruding oval footrim, the amber-colored body suffused with gold flecks, with a ruby-red overlay, well-carved to depict magpies amid flowering prunus branches, the footrim also carved from the overlay.
-The second, 19th/20th century, of flattened circular form, with a flat lip, waisted neck and shallow oval protruding footrim, the body dark ruby-red, with a well-carved sky-blue overlay, depicting on one main side a chilong clambering through a bi disc, bats flying above, the reverse with cranes and a pavilion among clouds emerging from a three-toed frog, all above waves. 
-The third, probably 20th century, of flattened pear-form with tall neck, flat lip, the opaque turquoise-geen body overlaid with black and yellow, carved with a goldfish among waterplants, verso with a crab and millet, underside with carved apocryphal Qianlong seal mark
-The fourth, 19th century, of tapering rounded-rectangular form, the shoulders sloping to a waisted neck, with a wide mouth, flat lip and protruding splayed oval footrim, the densely bubble-suffused body with black and caramel overlays depicting, on the main sides, lotus and Buddha's hand citron growing from antique vessels, the narrow sides with elongated mask-and-ring carvings, the footrim also carved from the overlay
-The fifth, 19th century, the five-color overlay glass of flattened ovoid form, the shoulders sloping to a slightly everted neck, with a flat lip and protruding oval footrim, the bubble-suffused bottle decorated with overlays in pink, red, blue and orange, carved as flowerheads connected by leafy green vines, the footrim also neatly carved from the green overlay
-The sixth, late 20th century. Double-overlay glass of pear-shape, the shoulders sloping to a slightly everted lipped neck, with a concave lip and protruding oval footrim, the striated cloudy-white and brown body thinly overlaid in caramel, covering the body with a geometric diaper-pattern ground and carved on the narrow sides with elongated mask-and-rings, as well as the footrim, and a second overlay on the main sides in dark brown to depict a groom pulling a reluctant horse, beneath lingzhi-shaped clouds.

Tallest height with stopper 3 1/4 in., 8.2 cm.

Property from the Estate of Dr. Thomas Klein, sold to benefit Jefferson Hospital

This lot is located in Philadelphia.

provenance: Property from the Estate of Dr. Thomas A. Klein, sold to benefit Jefferson Hospital
description_block:
Five Chinese Glass Snuff Bottles
料器鼻烟壺五支

-The first, probably 20th century, of flattened ovoid form with tapered neck, concave lip, raised on low oval foot, of amethyst glass carved in low relief with chilong against a ground of stylized waves, underside with apocryphal Qianlong mark
-The second, 20th century, of flattened ovoid form with waisted neck, concave lip, raised on low oval foot, of white cased with pink, cased with white, carved with lotus petals

Property from the Estate of Dr. Thomas Klein, sold to benefit Jefferson Hospital

description_block:
Four Chinese Blue Overlay Glass Snuff Bottles
涅白地套藍料鼻烟壺四支

-The first, late 19th/20th century, of double-gourd form, with a slightly waisted neck, concave lip and protruding circular footrim, the sapphire-blue overlay skillfully carved through to the milk-white ground, depicting a leafy vine with numerous gourds, the footrim also formed from the overlay.
-The second, late 19th century, of flattened circular form, the shoulders sloping to a cylindrical neck, with a flat lip and protruding oval footrim, the bubble-suffused body with a sapphire-blue overlay, well-carved to depict, on one main side, phoenix gazing up at the sun, the reverse with a pine tree, one narrow side with bamboo, the other with a blossoming prunus, the footrim also carved from the overlay.

Property from the Estate of Dr. Thomas A. Klein, MD., Sold to benefit the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at Thomas Jefferson University Hospital

This lot is located in Philadelphia.
Property from the Estate of Dr. Thomas A. Klein, MD. Sold to benefit the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at Thomas Jefferson University Hospital.來源：Thomas Klein醫生遺產，拍賣所得歸Jefferson醫院。湯姆·克萊因醫生收藏鼻烟壺逾四十年。他畢業於哈佛大學與羅徹斯特大學，曾於美國陸軍擔任婦產科醫師並出任高階領導職務。其後於傑佛遜醫院服務三十年，2023年以婦產科副主任身分榮退，期間培養了五百餘名住院醫師與無數醫學生。他的學術與臨床精神延續於以其名設立的「Thomas A. Klein 講席教授」，本場拍賣所得亦歸於傑佛遜醫院。Tom Klein’s life was shaped by two enduring passions: medicine and the collecting of snuff bottles. While these worlds rarely intersected, both were marked by the same qualities—quiet dedication, discernment, and grace. Tom was unfailingly modest–when the I.C.S.B.S. held its convention in Philadelphia, he entrusted me to select bottles from his collection for the exhibition “Embers of the East,” a task made challenging by the number of exceptional bottles. His passion for collecting was thoughtful rather than acquisitive, grounded in appreciation rather than display. These were his companions—objects he handled, studied, and loved for over 40 years.Professionally, Tom enjoyed an equally distinguished career. A graduate of Harvard University and the University of Rochester, he served as an obstetrician-gynecologist in the U.S. Army in senior leadership roles. He spent thirty years at Jefferson Hospital, retiring in 2023 as Vice Chair of Obstetrics and Gynecology, having trained more than five hundred residents and countless medical students. His legacy continues through the Thomas A. Klein, MD Professorship in Quality and Safety in Women’s Health. To those who knew him as a collector, these accomplishments mirrored the man I admired: principled, generous, and exacting without pretension. Over the 35 years I had the privilege to know him, he was a gentleman in the most absolute sense of the word. Though he is deeply missed, his presence endures in the objects he cherished and in our shared love of snuff bottles.Clare Chu

宣統三年正月時中書局印《錢牧齋箋註杜詩》

Length 10 1/4 x Width 6 1/4 in., 26 x 16 cm.

This lot is located in Chicago.
Property from the collection of Xiwen (Yiling) Wang, thence by descent.Wang Xiwen (also known as Wang Yiling) was born in 1881 in Neijiang, Sichuan. In his early years, he studied in Japan, where he befriended fellow Sichuan native and renowned painter Zhang Daqian. Upon returning to China, he was invited by Zhou Zuomin to join the Kincheng Banking Corporation (Jincheng Yinhang), serving successively as branch manager in Hankou, Beijing, and Tianjin. A prominent banker during the Republican Period, Wang was also a passionate collector of calligraphy, paintings, and rubbings, assembling a collection that remains partially preserved today in the Shanghai Museum and Shanghai Library.In his later years, Wang settled in Hong Kong, while his children dispersed to Taiwan, Brazil, and the United States. Through these family networks, portions of the collection have appeared at auction in recent years. In April 2022, Sotheby’s Hong Kong featured two works by Zhang Daqian (lots 3170 and 3171) from the Wang collection in their Classical Chinese Painting auction; both were gifted by Zhang to Wang’s second son, Wang Yixian, during his time at the famed Garden of Eight Virtues (Bade Yuan) in Brazil. Wang Yixian resided nearby and assisted Zhang in shipping and exporting his paintings. In May 2024, Heffel Auctions in Toronto offered another Zhang painting from a different branch of the Wang family. In October 2024, at Duoyunxuan Auction in Shanghai, lots 1453–1527 also came from the Wang family, featuring Shanghai School masters and rubbings that had been returned to the family after being seized during the Cultural Revolution in the 1970s.The present collection, comprising paintings and books from the Wang family, is consigned by the grandchildren.來源：銀行家王錫文（1881-1955）舊藏。王錫文字毅靈、毅厂，1882年生於四川內江。早年留學日本，因此結識同在東瀛的四川老鄉張大千，歸國后，受周作民邀請加入金城銀行，先後在漢口、北京、天津等地擔任分行經理。銀行家是民國時期重要的收藏團體，王錫文喜好碑帖書畫，部分藏品現存上海博物館及上海圖書館。晚年定居香港，子女分散臺灣、巴西、北美。是以近年拍場時見其舊藏，如2022年4月香港蘇富比中國書畫專場3170、3171號張大千《松崖白練》、《白蓮》，即爲大千巴西“八德園”時期贈予王錫文次子王宜憲的作品，此子僑居巴西摩詰，與大千比鄰，曾助大千運送、出口畫作，有世交之誼。2024年5月多倫多Heffel拍賣的大千《松崖高逸》則來自另一位王家後人。2024年10月朵雲軒秋拍1453-1527號拍品也是王家舊藏，以海派名家和舊拓爲主，係八十年代退賠。

Property from the Collection of George C.T. Wan, New York, thence by descent.George Chien-Tze ("C.T.") Wan was born in Jiangxi province, of China. He became interested in Chinese porcelains when, in Shanghai, Mr. Wan worked as a representative for importers of Chinese porcelains to the United States. Through this work, he obtained sponsorship to immigrate to the United States in 1949. Within a year, C.T. Wan & Co., dealer in Chinese art and antiques, was inaugurated in New York City at 116 East 28th St. Thus began a dedication and passion for Asian art and collecting that was to fulfill Mr. Wan's excellent life until his passing in 2019. The store moved twice, first a few blocks away to 235 Fifth Avenue in the 1960's and then across the avenue in the 1980's to 242 Fifth Avenue. In the 2000’s, surrounded by his collection, Mr. Wan would smile and reflect on what great satisfaction and pride his life's work had brought to him.來源：萬寶古董行庫藏。該行由江西籍古董商萬氏創立，萬氏上世紀中葉在滬從事瓷器出口貿易，1949年移民紐約，于28街東116號經營瓷器，店名C.T. Wan & Co，后遷五大道235號，再遷242號。店址雖多次變動，都位於五大道與28街交匯處，這是當年紐約亞洲藝術交易的中心，如山中商會就在254號，與萬寶古董行一街之隔。千禧年后，萬氏年高，淡出經營，2019年下世，本次上拍子女繼承的部分庫存。

Property from the Collection of George C.T. Wan, New York, thence by descent.George Chien-Tze ("C.T.") Wan was born in Jiangxi province, of China. He became interested in Chinese porcelains when, in Shanghai, Mr. Wan worked as a representative for importers of Chinese porcelains to the United States. Through this work, he obtained sponsorship to immigrate to the United States in 1949. Within a year, C.T. Wan & Co., dealer in Chinese art and antiques, was inaugurated in New York City at 116 East 28th St. Thus began a dedication and passion for Asian art and collecting that was to fulfill Mr. Wan's excellent life until his passing in 2019. The store moved twice, first a few blocks away to 235 Fifth Avenue in the 1960's and then across the avenue in the 1980's to 242 Fifth Avenue. In the 2000’s, surrounded by his collection, Mr. Wan would smile and reflect on what great satisfaction and pride his life's work had brought to him.來源：萬寶古董行庫藏。該行由江西籍古董商萬氏創立，萬氏上世紀中葉在滬從事瓷器出口貿易，1949年移民紐約，于28街東116號經營瓷器，店名C.T. Wan & Co，后遷五大道235號，再遷242號。店址雖多次變動，都位於五大道與28街交匯處，這是當年紐約亞洲藝術交易的中心，如山中商會就在254號，與萬寶古董行一街之隔。千禧年后，萬氏年高，淡出經營，2019年下世，本次上拍子女繼承的部分庫存。

Wang and the renowned calligrapher and scholar Wang Fangyu, both of whom exhibited their work at the Frankel gallery. He has particularly fond memories of fascinating discussions with the psychologist and television personality Dr. Ruth Westheimer, who was a dear friend of the Frankel’s and wrote an essay for the catalogue for their Exhibition called “Play It Again, Asian Games and Pastimes” which received much attention including a significant review in the New York Times. A collector of antiquarian books and Asian art since his youth, Mr. Butterman is a distinguished attorney and has, in his long career, represented numerous important artists, galleries, and collectors in a variety of capacities.  We are privileged to present these important pieces in addition to early Chinese ceramics, other scholarly items, and Japanese works of art from Mr. Butterman’s collection.來源：紐約州紐約市Jay R. Property from the estate of Rafeeuddin Ahmed, New York, New York.Mr. Rafeeuddin Ahmed had a long and distinguished diplomatic career, serving with the Pakistan Foreign Service from 1955-1969, and in 1970 embarked on the first of several distinguished roles within the United Nations Secretariat, spanning over 30 years. Between 1955 and 1968, he served at the Embassies of Cairo, Ottawa, and Beijing. Mr. Ahmed was highly respected by colleagues and those who came to know him. He was a valued mentor and a great believer in the power of multilateralism and international cooperation, and, as a tribute from the World Tourism Organization (UN Tourism) notes, “…leaving behind a legacy defined not only by institutional achievement, but by humanity, wisdom and grace.”来源：纽约市外交家拉菲乌丁·艾哈迈德（Rafeeuddin Ahmed，1932—2026）遗产。巴基斯坦资深外交家艾哈迈德供职于联合国体系逾三十年，以副秘书长级别工作二十一年，是国际多边外交领域的重要人物之一。艾氏毕业于巴基斯坦旁遮普大学，后赴美国塔夫茨大学深造，专攻国际经济与国际法。1954年他以政治学讲师身份开启职业生涯，次年加入巴基斯坦外交部，1955至1969年间先后派驻开罗、渥太华及北京等地。1970年进入联合国秘书处，历任开发计划署高级顾问、经济及社会理事会秘书、秘书长办公厅主任、亚太经济社会委员会执行秘书等职。艾氏多次受命处理复杂国际事务，参与过东帝汶、柬埔寨、老挝—泰国冲突及缅甸等地区的调停。在1982年福克兰群岛危机和伊朗人质事件中发挥了重要作用。2003年又被任命为伊拉克问题特别顾问。他在2026年逝世，一生成就卓著，评价极高。本场委托的中国艺术品购自1960年代派驻北京巴基斯坦使馆任内。

Property from the Collection of Esther Haviland Farrior (1921–1996) and John Farrior (1920–1989), New York.The Haviland–Farrior Collection was formed by Esther Underhill Haviland Farrior (1921–1996) and John McMullen Farrior (1920–1989), whose lives were deeply intertwined with China during a period of profound historical transition. The majority of the works were acquired in China between 1947 and 1950 and have since descended within the family. Property from the Collection of Esther Haviland Farrior (1921–1996) and John Farrior (1920–1989), New York.The Haviland–Farrior Collection was formed by Esther Underhill Haviland Farrior (1921–1996) and John McMullen Farrior (1920–1989), whose lives were deeply intertwined with China during a period of profound historical transition. The majority of the works were acquired in China between 1947 and 1950 and have since descended within the family. Esther Haviland Farrior belonged to the inaugural cohort of Fulbright scholars in China. After completing graduate study in Chinese studies at Columbia University under Professor Carrington Goodrich (傅路德), she traveled to Beijing in 1947 and enrolled at Tsinghua University, where she studied ancient Chinese inscriptions under the eminent scholar Chen Mengjia (陳夢家). Specializing in Shang dynasty oracle bones and early bronze culture, she pursued research at a moment when the intellectual and political landscape of China was rapidly shifting. As Communist forces approached Beijing in 1948, she relocated to the Tsinghua campus to continue her studies, supporting herself by teaching English while remaining immersed in archaeological research.Her relationship with Chen Mengjia extended well beyond the seminar room. In July 1949, when Esther married John McMullen Farrior in a garden ceremony in Beijing, it was Chen Mengjia who walked her down the aisle. Their wedding invitation was preserved among Chen’s personal papers, later encountered by scholars researching his life and work. John McMullen Farrior, raised in China as the son of Presbyterian missionaries who lived there from 1910 to 1949, returned to Beijing in 1948 as a career U.S. Foreign Service Officer. Following their marriage, the couple’s diplomatic postings took them across East and Southeast Asia, including Seoul, Bangkok, Hong Kong, Kuala Lumpur, Tokyo, and Ankara. Throughout decades of movement across cultures, they continued to collect with discernment and scholarly sensitivity.Shaped by Esther’s archaeological training and John’s lifelong familiarity with China, the Haviland–Farrior Collection reflects not only aesthetic appreciation but lived experience. It stands as a testament to a generation of scholars and diplomats whose personal histories were inseparable from the cultural worlds they inhabited.來源：Esther Underhill Haviland Farrior（1921–1996）與 John McMullen Farrior（1920–1989）夫婦遺產。1947-1950年間購於中國，此後家族遞藏。Esther Haviland Farrior 為最早一批赴華的傅爾布萊特學者。早年就讀於哥倫比亞大學，師從漢學先驅傅路德（Carrington Goodrich），1947年前往北京，入清華大學，師從著名學者陳夢家，研習商代甲骨文與早期青銅文化。她與陳夢家的關係不僅止於師生。1949年7月，Esther 與 John McMullen Farrior 於北京成婚，陳夢家主婚，牽著她步入禮堂。婚禮請柬保存於陳夢家的私人檔案，後來成為研究其生平的學者所見的史料之一。John McMullen Farrior 出生長老會傳教士之家，父母于20世紀早期長期駐扎中國，從事傳教活動於中國。1948年他以美國外交官身分重返北京任職。婚後，夫婦二人隨外交任命輾轉東亞與東南亞多地，包括首爾、曼谷、香港、吉隆坡、東京與安卡拉。所蓄藏品見證了一代學者與外交官的生命軌跡，個人歷史與所置身的文化世界密不可分。

Property from the estate of Rafeeuddin Ahmed, New York, New York.Mr. Rafeeuddin Ahmed had a long and distinguished diplomatic career, serving with the Pakistan Foreign Service from 1955-1969, and in 1970 embarked on the first of several distinguished roles within the United Nations Secretariat, spanning over 30 years. Between 1955 and 1968, he served at the Embassies of Cairo, Ottawa, and Beijing. Mr. Ahmed was highly respected by colleagues and those who came to know him. He was a valued mentor and a great believer in the power of multilateralism and international cooperation, and, as a tribute from the World Tourism Organization (UN Tourism) notes, “…leaving behind a legacy defined not only by institutional achievement, but by humanity, wisdom and grace.”来源：纽约市外交家拉菲乌丁·艾哈迈德（Rafeeuddin Ahmed，1932—2026）遗产。巴基斯坦资深外交家艾哈迈德供职于联合国体系逾三十年，以副秘书长级别工作二十一年，是国际多边外交领域的重要人物之一。艾氏毕业于巴基斯坦旁遮普大学，后赴美国塔夫茨大学深造，专攻国际经济与国际法。1954年他以政治学讲师身份开启职业生涯，次年加入巴基斯坦外交部，1955至1969年间先后派驻开罗、渥太华及北京等地。1970年进入联合国秘书处，历任开发计划署高级顾问、经济及社会理事会秘书、秘书长办公厅主任、亚太经济社会委员会执行秘书等职。艾氏多次受命处理复杂国际事务，参与过东帝汶、柬埔寨、老挝—泰国冲突及缅甸等地区的调停。在1982年福克兰群岛危机和伊朗人质事件中发挥了重要作用。2003年又被任命为伊拉克问题特别顾问。他在2026年逝世，一生成就卓著，评价极高。本场委托的中国艺术品购自1960年代派驻北京巴基斯坦使馆任内。

Property from the Collection of George C.T. Wan, New York, thence by descent.George Chien-Tze ("C.T.") Wan was born in Jiangxi province, of China. He became interested in Chinese porcelains when, in Shanghai, Mr. Wan worked as a representative for importers of Chinese porcelains to the United States. Through this work, he obtained sponsorship to immigrate to the United States in 1949. Within a year, C.T. Wan & Co., dealer in Chinese art and antiques, was inaugurated in New York City at 116 East 28th St. Thus began a dedication and passion for Asian art and collecting that was to fulfill Mr. Wan's excellent life until his passing in 2019. The store moved twice, first a few blocks away to 235 Fifth Avenue in the 1960's and then across the avenue in the 1980's to 242 Fifth Avenue. In the 2000’s, surrounded by his collection, Mr. Wan would smile and reflect on what great satisfaction and pride his life's work had brought to him.來源：萬寶古董行庫藏。該行由江西籍古董商萬氏創立，萬氏上世紀中葉在滬從事瓷器出口貿易，1949年移民紐約，于28街東116號經營瓷器，店名C.T. Wan & Co，后遷五大道235號，再遷242號。店址雖多次變動，都位於五大道與28街交匯處，這是當年紐約亞洲藝術交易的中心，如山中商會就在254號，與萬寶古董行一街之隔。千禧年后，萬氏年高，淡出經營，2019年下世，本次上拍子女繼承的部分庫存。

Two Japanese Porcelain Chargers

Property from the Estate of George Burrows, Illinois.George Burrows was a gentleman in every sense of the word. Born in Chicago and raised in nearby Park Ridge, his mother maintained a lovely home furnished with antiques, many of which he inherited and treasured in his own collection. He spent summers during his childhood and teen years in Mackinac Island, Michigan, where he later restored his family’s home to a masterpiece. He graduated from the University of Miami and continued to spend much of his time in Florida throughout his life. As a young man, he went to work building his family business, The Burrows Company, and expanded it significantly over the years until he sold the company in 2009. While he was a tireless worker, he found time for extensive travel and took thirteen trips on the Concorde Supersonic Airliner to Paris and London. He also regularly made trips to New York City to maintain his immaculate and beautifully tailored wardrobe. Mr. Burrows enjoyed fine hotels, fine dining, and elegant surroundings. The collection offered by Freeman’s | Hindman reflects his refined taste for objects and works of art that were cherished in his homes for decades. More property from the Estate of George Burrows will be offered in Freeman’s | Hindman’s upcoming European Furniture and Decorative Arts auction on February 11, 2025.

Property from the Estate of Dr. Thomas A. Klein, MD. Sold to benefit the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at Thomas Jefferson University Hospital. Thomas Klein醫生遺產，拍賣所得歸Jefferson醫院。湯姆·克萊因醫生收藏鼻烟壺逾四十年。他畢業於哈佛大學與羅徹斯特大學，曾於美國陸軍擔任婦產科醫師並出任高階領導職務。其後於傑佛遜醫院服務三十年，2023年以婦產科副主任身分榮退，期間培養了五百餘名住院醫師與無數醫學生。他的學術與臨床精神延續於以其名設立的「Thomas A. Klein 講席教授」，本場拍賣所得亦歸於傑佛遜醫院。Tom Klein’s life was shaped by two enduring passions: medicine and the collecting of snuff bottles. While these worlds rarely intersected, both were marked by the same qualities—quiet dedication, discernment, and grace. Tom was unfailingly modest–when the I.C.S.B.S. held its convention in Philadelphia, he entrusted me to select bottles from his collection for the exhibition “Embers of the East,” a task made challenging by the number of exceptional bottles. His passion for collecting was thoughtful rather than acquisitive, grounded in appreciation rather than display. These were his companions—objects he handled, studied, and loved for over 40 years.Professionally, Tom enjoyed an equally distinguished career. A graduate of Harvard University and the University of Rochester, he served as an obstetrician-gynecologist in the U.S. Army in senior leadership roles. He spent thirty years at Jefferson Hospital, retiring in 2023 as Vice Chair of Obstetrics and Gynecology, having trained more than five hundred residents and countless medical students. His legacy continues through the Thomas A. Klein, MD Professorship in Quality and Safety in Women’s Health. To those who knew him as a collector, these accomplishments mirrored the man I admired: principled, generous, and exacting without pretension. Over the 35 years I had the privilege to know him, he was a gentleman in the most absolute sense of the word. Though he is deeply missed, his presence endures in the objects he cherished and in our shared love of snuff bottles.Clare Chu

Property from the estate of Rafeeuddin Ahmed, New York, New York.Mr. Rafeeuddin Ahmed had a long and distinguished diplomatic career, serving with the Pakistan Foreign Service from 1955-1969, and in 1970 embarked on the first of several distinguished roles within the United Nations Secretariat, spanning over 30 years. Between 1955 and 1968, he served at the Embassies of Cairo, Ottawa, and Beijing. Mr. Ahmed was highly respected by colleagues and those who came to know him. He was a valued mentor and a great believer in the power of multilateralism and international cooperation, and, as a tribute from the World Tourism Organization (UN Tourism) notes, “…leaving behind a legacy defined not only by institutional achievement, but by humanity, wisdom and grace.”来源：纽约市外交家拉菲乌丁·艾哈迈德（Rafeeuddin Ahmed，1932—2026）遗产。巴基斯坦资深外交家艾哈迈德供职于联合国体系逾三十年，以副秘书长级别工作二十一年，是国际多边外交领域的重要人物之一。艾氏毕业于巴基斯坦旁遮普大学，后赴美国塔夫茨大学深造，专攻国际经济与国际法。1954年他以政治学讲师身份开启职业生涯，次年加入巴基斯坦外交部，1955至1969年间先后派驻开罗、渥太华及北京等地。1970年进入联合国秘书处，历任开发计划署高级顾问、经济及社会理事会秘书、秘书长办公厅主任、亚太经济社会委员会执行秘书等职。艾氏多次受命处理复杂国际事务，参与过东帝汶、柬埔寨、老挝—泰国冲突及缅甸等地区的调停。在1982年福克兰群岛危机和伊朗人质事件中发挥了重要作用。2003年又被任命为伊拉克问题特别顾问。他在2026年逝世，一生成就卓著，评价极高。本场委托的中国艺术品购自1960年代派驻北京巴基斯坦使馆任内。

Property from the estate of Rafeeuddin Ahmed, New York, New York.Mr. Rafeeuddin Ahmed had a long and distinguished diplomatic career, serving with the Pakistan Foreign Service from 1955-1969, and in 1970 embarked on the first of several distinguished roles within the United Nations Secretariat, spanning over 30 years. Between 1955 and 1968, he served at the Embassies of Cairo, Ottawa, and Beijing. Mr. Ahmed was highly respected by colleagues and those who came to know him. He was a valued mentor and a great believer in the power of multilateralism and international cooperation, and, as a tribute from the World Tourism Organization (UN Tourism) notes, “…leaving behind a legacy defined not only by institutional achievement, but by humanity, wisdom and grace.”来源：纽约市外交家拉菲乌丁·艾哈迈德（Rafeeuddin Ahmed，1932—2026）遗产。巴基斯坦资深外交家艾哈迈德供职于联合国体系逾三十年，以副秘书长级别工作二十一年，是国际多边外交领域的重要人物之一。艾氏毕业于巴基斯坦旁遮普大学，后赴美国塔夫茨大学深造，专攻国际经济与国际法。1954年他以政治学讲师身份开启职业生涯，次年加入巴基斯坦外交部，1955至1969年间先后派驻开罗、渥太华及北京等地。1970年进入联合国秘书处，历任开发计划署高级顾问、经济及社会理事会秘书、秘书长办公厅主任、亚太经济社会委员会执行秘书等职。艾氏多次受命处理复杂国际事务，参与过东帝汶、柬埔寨、老挝—泰国冲突及缅甸等地区的调停。在1982年福克兰群岛危机和伊朗人质事件中发挥了重要作用。2003年又被任命为伊拉克问题特别顾问。他在2026年逝世，一生成就卓著，评价极高。本场委托的中国艺术品购自1960年代派驻北京巴基斯坦使馆任内。
